l:akkusativ:0:body: These prepositions (durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, entlang) always require the accusative case. With entlang the noun often precedes the preposition, e.g., den Fluss entlang.
l:akkusativ:0:ex1: The gift is für meinen Bruder.
l:akkusativ:0:title: The Fixed Accusative Prepositions
l:akkusativ:1:body: In the accusative, the definite articles are den (masculine), die (feminine), das (neuter), and die (plural). The personal pronouns are mich, dich, ihn, sie, es, uns, euch, sie.
l:akkusativ:1:title: Articles and Pronouns
l:akkusativ:2:body: The prepositions für, gegen, bis, and um take the accusative case. Für indicates purpose or a time span, gegen expresses an approximate time or contrast, bis marks a limit, and um denotes a location around something or a specific time.
l:akkusativ:2:ex0: I am studying for the exam.
l:akkusativ:2:ex2: The children sit around the table.
l:akkusativ:2:title: Time, Purpose, and Direction
l:akkusativ:3:body: The preposition ohne never takes the dative; it requires the accusative (e.g., ohne den Regenschirm, not ohne dem Regenschirm). With für, the article agrees with the noun's gender and case (e.g., für meinen Vater, für meine Mutter).
l:akkusativ:3:title: Common Mistakes
l:akkusativ:intro: Accusative prepositions always require the accusative case. They indicate direction, purpose, contrast, duration, or lack of accompaniment.
l:dativ-akkusativ:0:body: With verbs like geben, schenken, zeigen, and erklären, the person receives the dative case and the thing receives the accusative case. Example: Ich gebe dem Freund das Buch.
l:dativ-akkusativ:0:ex0: She shows the teacher the exercise.
l:dativ-akkusativ:0:ex1: I give my sister a book.
l:dativ-akkusativ:0:ex2: He explains the rule to the children.
l:dativ-akkusativ:0:title: Recipient and Object
l:dativ-akkusativ:1:body: When both objects are pronouns, the accusative comes before the dative: Ich gebe es ihm. When both are nouns, the dative usually comes before the accusative: Ich gebe dem Freund das Buch.
l:dativ-akkusativ:1:ex2: She explains it to the children.
l:dativ-akkusativ:1:title: Order of Pronouns
l:dativ-akkusativ:2:body: Some verbs require the dative case even when no recipient is obvious, such as helfen, danken, folgen, gehören, gefallen, passen, and antworten. These verbs must be learned together with their case.
l:dativ-akkusativ:2:title: Verbs with Fixed Dative
l:dativ-akkusativ:3:body: Prepositions such as mit, nach, aus, bei, von, zu, and seit require the dative, while durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, and bis require the accusative. With two-way prepositions, the choice depends on whether you ask Wo? (where) or Wohin? (where to).
l:dativ-akkusativ:3:ex2: I put the book on the table.
l:dativ-akkusativ:3:title: Prepositions Determine Case
l:dativ-akkusativ:intro: Dative and accusative are chosen based on their role in the sentence, not from a word list: the dative is often the recipient, the accusative the direct object.
l:dativ:0:body: The most important are mit, nach, aus, bei, von, zu, seit, and gegenüber. They never change case: even with movement they stay in the dative.
l:dativ:0:title: Fixed Dative Prepositions
l:dativ:1:body: In the dative case, the definite article is "dem" for masculine and neuter, "der" for feminine, and "den" for plural. The personal pronouns are "mir", "dir", "ihm", "ihr", "ihm", "uns", "euch", "ihnen".
l:dativ:1:ex2: The book belongs to the children.
l:dativ:1:title: Articles and Pronouns in the Dative
l:dativ:2:body: Prepositions often merge with the definite article: "zu" + "dem" = "zum", "zu" + "der" = "zur", "von" + "dem" = "vom", "bei" + "dem" = "beim". These forms are standard, not colloquial.
l:dativ:2:title: Contractions with the Article
l:dativ:3:body: After these prepositions the accusative is wrong. Also note "seit": it is used with the present tense when the action continues to the present, e.g. "Ich wohne seit einem Jahr hier".
l:dativ:3:ex0: I have been learning German for a month.
l:dativ:3:ex1: We are talking with the teacher.
l:dativ:3:ex2: The café is located opposite the museum.
l:dativ:3:title: Common Mistakes
l:dativ:intro: Dative prepositions always require the dative case. The dative often marks the recipient, location, or reference of an action.
l:genitiv:0:body: The genitive answers the question "Wessen?" (whose?), as in das Auto meines Bruders or die Farbe des Hauses. It often follows a noun, but can also appear after sein, werden, and certain verbs such as bedürfen, gedenken, or sich bewusst sein.
l:genitiv:0:ex1: I like the color of the house.
l:genitiv:0:title: What is the genitive used for?
l:genitiv:1:body: Masculine and neuter nouns take des; feminine and plural take der. Masculine and neuter nouns often add -s or -es: des Mannes, des Kindes, des Autos. One-syllable nouns usually take -es, multi-syllable nouns often take -s.
l:genitiv:1:title: Articles and nouns in the genitive
l:genitiv:2:body: After des/der the adjective takes the genitive ending (e.g., des neuen Autos). Possessive articles agree with the owner and with the gender, number, and case of the possessed noun.
l:genitiv:2:ex0: the end of the long film
l:genitiv:2:ex1: the opinion of my best friend
l:genitiv:2:ex2: the doors of our new apartment
l:genitiv:2:title: Adjectives and Possessive Articles
l:genitiv:3:body: Prepositions such as wegen, trotz, während, statt, innerhalb, außerhalb, aufgrund, anlässlich, hinsichtlich, ungeachtet, oberhalb, unterhalb, diesseits, jenseits, kraft, and zwecks require the genitive in standard German. In colloquial speech the dative sometimes appears, but for B1/B2 the genitive is the correct written form.
l:genitiv:3:ex0: Because of the storm, the train stops.
l:genitiv:3:ex1: Despite the cold, we go for a walk.
l:genitiv:3:ex2: Within the deadline, the registration is valid.
l:genitiv:3:title: Prepositions with Genitive
l:genitiv:4:body: Dessen and deren replace a genitive and refer to a person or thing, e.g., der Mann, dessen Auto hier steht; die Frau, deren Sohn krank ist. In everyday German, von + dative often replaces the genitive, e.g., das Auto von meinem Bruder, which is understandable but less formal.
l:genitiv:4:ex0: The author whose book I am reading is coming tomorrow.
l:genitiv:4:ex1: The colleague whose idea won is sick.
l:genitiv:4:title: dessen, deren, and the von-replacement form
l:genitiv:intro: The genitive case expresses possession, belonging, and reference, and it follows key prepositions like wegen, trotz, während, statt, and innerhalb; correct article, adjective, and noun endings are essential.
l:verben-praepositionen:0:body: Typical combinations are warten auf, denken an, sich interessieren für, teilnehmen an, sich freuen auf, Angst haben vor and sich erinnern an. The preposition cannot be freely replaced.
l:verben-praepositionen:0:ex0: We are waiting for the bus.
l:verben-praepositionen:0:title: Recognizing Fixed Combinations
l:verben-praepositionen:1:body: warten auf, denken an, sich interessieren für and sich erinnern an take the accusative. teilnehmen an, Angst haben vor and sich freuen über take the dative. Learn the preposition and case together.
l:verben-praepositionen:1:ex0: I am taking part in the course.
l:verben-praepositionen:1:ex1: He is afraid of the dog.
l:verben-praepositionen:1:ex2: We are happy about the gift.
l:verben-praepositionen:1:title: Which Case Goes with It?
l:verben-praepositionen:2:body: For things you ask with worauf, woran, wofür, or womit and answer with darauf, daran, dafür, or damit. For people you ask with auf wen, an wen, or für wen.
l:verben-praepositionen:2:title: Questions with wo- and da-
l:verben-praepositionen:3:body: Do not translate the preposition from your native language. For example, ‘Ich warte für den Bus’ is wrong; the correct form is ‘Ich warte auf den Bus’. Likewise, ‘Ich interessiere mich an Musik’ is wrong; the correct preposition is ‘für Musik’.
l:verben-praepositionen:3:title: Common Mistakes
l:verben-praepositionen:intro: Many verbs have a fixed preposition. This combination must be learned as a unit because the preposition determines the case and often the meaning.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:body: When describing a fixed position, the noun after a two-way preposition takes the dative. Typical verbs are sein, bleiben, liegen, stehen, sitzen, and hängen (in a state).
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:ex0: The book lies on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:ex1: The cat sleeps under the sofa.
l:wechselpraepositionen:0:title: Wo? — Static position
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:body: When describing movement toward a goal, the noun takes the accusative. Typical verbs are gehen, fahren, legen, stellen, setzen, and hängen (as an action).
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:ex0: I put the book on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:ex1: The cat jumps under the sofa.
l:wechselpraepositionen:1:title: Wohin? — Movement to a goal
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:body: Many verb pairs distinguish state and action: liegen/legen, stehen/stellen, sitzen/setzen, hängen/hängen. The case depends not only on the preposition but also on the verb's meaning.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex0: The bottle stands on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex1: I put the bottle on the table.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:ex2: The picture hangs on the wall.
l:wechselpraepositionen:2:title: The verb also decides
l:wechselpraepositionen:3:body: Common contractions include in+dem=im, an+dem=am, in+das=ins, an+das=ans; "nach Hause" and "zu Hause" do not use a two-way preposition. Always ask first: Wo? or Wohin?
l:wechselpraepositionen:3:title: Contractions and typical mistakes
l:wechselpraepositionen:intro: The nine two-way prepositions take the dative when describing a position (Wo?) and the accusative when describing movement toward a destination (Wohin?).
m:akkusativ:summary: These prepositions always require the accusative case. They include durch, für, gegen, ohne, um, bis, and entlang.
m:akkusativ:title: Prepositions with Accusative
m:dativ-akkusativ:summary: Choose dative or accusative based on the word's role in the sentence, not by memorizing a list.
m:dativ-akkusativ:title: Dative or Accusative?
m:dativ:summary: The prepositions mit, nach, aus, bei, von, zu, seit, and gegenüber always take the dative case.
m:dativ:title: Prepositions with Dative
m:genitiv:summary: This section covers prepositions that require the genitive case, such as wegen, trotz, während, statt, and innerhalb.
m:genitiv:title: Prepositions with Genitive
m:verben-praepositionen:summary: Verbs with fixed prepositions such as warten auf, sich interessieren für, teilnehmen an and their cases.
m:verben-praepositionen:title: Verbs with Fixed Prepositions
m:wechselpraepositionen:summary: The nine two-way prepositions (in, an, auf, unter, über, vor, hinter, neben, zwischen) take the dative for location (Wo?) and the accusative for direction (Wohin?).
